entries.title: Dolt Shared Server Recovery — Coordinated Restart Procedure
entries.summary:
When the shared Dolt server dies in a multi-rig Gas Town deployment,
bd auto-start creates rogue servers from each rig's .beads/dolt directory.
Recovery requires a coordinated shutdown to prevent the thundering herd.
entries.details:
## Symptoms
- gt mail inbox fails with "database beads_hq not found"
- gt dolt status says "not running" but port 3307 is in use
- /usr/sbin/lsof -p <pid> -Fn shows cwd is NOT ~/gt/.dolt-data
- mysql SHOW DATABASES only returns dolt, information_schema, mysql
## Diagnosis
1. Check what's on port 3307:
   /usr/sbin/lsof -i :3307 | grep LISTEN
2. Verify it's a rogue (cwd should be ~/gt/.dolt-data, not a rig's .beads/dolt):
   /usr/sbin/lsof -p <PID> -Fn | head -3
3. If cwd is any rig's .beads/dolt → it's a rogue
## Recovery (MUST follow this order)
1. STOP all rigs first to prevent respawning:
   gt rig stop rally_tavern myndy_api meety_me vitalitek myndy_ios gastown
   (Use --force if needed for rigs with uncommitted polecat work)
2. Kill ALL dolt processes:
   pkill -9 -f "dolt sql-server"
3. Verify port is free:
   /usr/sbin/lsof -i :3307  # Should show no LISTEN entries
4. Start correct server:
gotchas: bd auto-starts a local Dolt server from cwd when it can't connect
In multi-rig deployments, this creates N competing servers on port 3307
Each rogue only serves its own rig's database, not the shared set
gt dolt status checks PID file, not actual process — may report wrong state
Vitalitek or other rigs may refuse gt rig stop if polecats have uncommitted work

entries.title: Gas Town Beads Workflow
entries.summary: Best practices for using Beads with Gas Town for multi-agent work.
entries.details:
1. Use hash-based IDs (bd-abc12) to prevent merge conflicts
2. Set issue_prefix per rig to namespace beads
3. Use bd ready to find unblocked work
4. Claim atomically with bd claim before starting
5. Use hooks for persistent state across sessions
gotchas: Don't use hyphens in rig names (use underscores)
Dolt server must be running for full persistence
Compact old beads periodically to save context

entries.title: Gas Town Deacon Plugin System
entries.summary: How to use and write Deacon plugins for automated town maintenance.
entries.details:
Gas Town ships a plugin system that lets the Deacon run recurring automation
tasks during its patrol cycle. Plugins live in ~/gt/plugins/ (town-level) or
<rig>/plugins/ (rig-level) as directories containing a plugin.md file with
TOML frontmatter.
## Plugin Format
```
+++
name = "my-plugin"
description = "What this plugin does"
version = 1
[gate]
type = "cooldown"   # or: cron, condition, event, manual
duration = "1h"     # for cooldown gate
[tracking]
labels = ["plugin:my-plugin", "category:maintenance"]
digest = true
[execution]
timeout = "5m"
notify_on_failure = true
severity = "medium"   # low, medium, high, critical
gotchas: Plugin version must be an integer (1), not a string ("1") — TOML parser
Town-level plugins (~/gt/plugins/) apply to all rigs. Rig-level plugins
Deacon must be running for plugins to execute automatically. Use

entries.title: Gas Town — refinery/rig/.beads/redirect Setup for New Rigs
entries.summary:
New rigs need refinery/rig/.beads/redirect pointing to the rig's actual
.beads database. Missing this file causes gt patrol new to fail with
"database not initialized: issue_prefix config is missing".
entries.details:
## The Pattern
Gas Town's gt patrol new resolves the beads database from the refinery agent's
working directory by looking for refinery/rig/.beads/. If that directory only
contains a "redirect" file, gt follows the redirect path to find the real DB.
The redirect path is resolved relative to the rig/ directory (NOT from inside
.beads/). So for a rig where .beads lives at the rig root:
  refinery/rig/.beads/redirect → "../../.beads"
Resolves as: from refinery/rig/ → up two levels → rig root → .beads ✓
## Setup Steps
```bash
mkdir -p ~/gt/<rig>/refinery/rig/.beads
echo -n "../../.beads" > ~/gt/<rig>/refinery/rig/.beads/redirect
```
## Rig Variations
Different rigs place their .beads at different depths:
| Rig type | .beads location | redirect content |
|----------|----------------|------------------|
| Standard (source at rig root) | <rig>/.beads | ../../.beads |
| Gastown-style (source in mayor/rig) | <rig>/mayor/rig/.beads | ../../mayor/rig/.beads |
## Verification
gotchas: echo -n is required — trailing newline in the redirect file breaks resolution
The path is relative to the rig/ directory, not the .beads/ directory
gt unsling / gt patrol fail silently with wrong redirect paths; check with bd list

entries.title: Security Audits in Gas Town
entries.summary: Three layers of security coverage for Gas Town workspaces: passive, active, and periodic.
entries.details:
Gas Town provides three distinct security mechanisms. Use all three for coverage
at different granularities and timings.
## Layer 1: Passive — shiny-secure formula
For any polecat work, use `shiny-secure` instead of `shiny` when slinging.
It wraps every implement and submit step with pre/post security scans
automatically via the `security-audit` aspect.
```bash
gt formula run shiny-secure --rig my-project --issue hq-abc12
```
The `security-audit` aspect inserts steps before and after implement/submit:
- Pre-scan: review scope for secrets/creds, check deps for known vulns
- Post-scan: SAST on new code, OWASP Top 10 check, secrets scan
This is the lowest-friction option — no extra configuration required.
## Layer 2: On-demand — mol-dog-security formula
For targeted audits of a specific rig (e.g., after onboarding new code, before
a release, or when investigating an alert):
```bash
gt formula run mol-dog-security --rig my-project
```

entries.title: Gas Town Package Upgrade Sequence
entries.summary: The correct order to upgrade gastown, dolt, and beads without breaking your town.
entries.details:
Upgrading Gas Town packages requires a specific sequence. Skipping steps leaves
agents running stale binaries or the town in a misconfigured state.
## Correct Sequence
1. Upgrade packages via Homebrew:
   ```bash
   brew upgrade gastown dolt beads
   ```
   Note: upgrading beads may also pull a new gastown version as a dependency.
2. Run the post-install migration:
   ```bash
   gt upgrade
   ```
   This runs `gt doctor --fix` internally, then syncs: formulas, CLAUDE.md,
   hooks, and daemon.json lifecycle defaults. It is idempotent — safe to run
   multiple times.
3. Restart all agents to pick up new binaries and config:
   ```bash
   gt up --restore
   ```
4. Verify everything came up:

entries.title: HIPAA Minimum Necessary — List vs Detail API Endpoints
entries.summary:
List endpoints (GET /resource) must return only the fields needed for display
(id, name). PII and PHI fields belong exclusively on detail endpoints
(GET /resource/:id). This directly satisfies HIPAA's minimum necessary standard.
entries.details:
## The Rule
HIPAA minimum necessary (45 CFR §164.502(b)) requires limiting PHI disclosure
to the minimum needed for the intended purpose. A user browsing a list does not
need full patient details — they need enough to identify and select a record.
## Field Split
| Endpoint | Allowed fields | Prohibited fields |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| GET /clients | id, first_name, last_name | dob, phone, email, insurance_payer, insurance_member_id, created_at |
| GET /clients/:id | All fields | — |
## Implementation
```python
# BAD — leaks PHI in list response
@router.get("/clients")
def list_clients():
    clients = db.query(Client).all()
    return [client.to_dict() for client in clients]  # includes all fields
# GOOD — minimum necessary
@router.get("/clients")
def list_clients():
    clients = db.query(Client).all()
gotchas: Audit existing list endpoints — they frequently include full model serialization
Search endpoints (GET /clients?q=name) are list endpoints — same restrictions apply
Logging middleware must not log response bodies for detail endpoints (would log PHI)
Frontend should not cache detail responses in shared/local storage

entries.title: iOS - Background Processing Reliability Patterns
entries.summary:
BGTaskScheduler tasks must be marked complete via real completion callbacks, not
asyncAfter timeouts. HealthKit sync should use HKObserverQuery (push-based) not
polling timers. Don't run multiple overlapping sync managers simultaneously.
entries.details:
## BGTask Completion
The most common mistake is marking BGAppRefreshTask/BGProcessingTask complete via
a hardcoded asyncAfter delay rather than waiting for the actual work to finish:
  BAD: DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 25) {
         task.setTaskCompleted(success: true)  // work may still be running!
       }
iOS uses task completion to schedule future background wakeups. If you signal
complete too early, iOS may suspend the process while sync is still in flight.
If you signal it late or never, iOS kills the process and deprioritizes future
wakeups.
GOOD: pass a completion handler into the sync operation and call
task.setTaskCompleted(success:) from within that handler. Add a safety timeout
that calls setTaskCompleted(success: false) only if the handler hasn't fired.
## HealthKit: Use Observer Queries, Not Timers
Polling HealthKit on a timer is wasteful and unreliable. iOS provides push-based
delivery via HKObserverQuery + enableBackgroundDelivery:
- App is woken in background when new health data arrives
- Combine with HKAnchoredObjectQuery for incremental (anchor-based) sync
- No timer needed — iOS does the scheduling
## Don't Run Multiple Sync Managers
gotchas: BGAppRefreshTask has ~30 seconds; BGProcessingTask has minutes but requires network/power flags
setTaskCompleted must be called before the task's expirationHandler fires, or iOS penalizes future scheduling
HKObserverQuery + enableBackgroundDelivery requires HealthKit background delivery entitlement in Xcode
Multiple CLLocationManager instances in one app share device GPS — creating 3 managers doesn't give you 3x accuracy, just 3x confusion
SyncScheduler + AutoSyncManager running simultaneously can both call syncAllHealthData() concurrently — HealthDataManager needs a re-entrancy guard

entries.title: iOS - Never Store Credentials in UserDefaults
entries.summary:
Auth tokens and passwords must live in the iOS Keychain, not UserDefaults.
UserDefaults are unencrypted on disk and accessible in unencrypted backups.
entries.details:
UserDefaults data is stored in plaintext in the app container at
Library/Preferences/<bundle-id>.plist. It is included in unencrypted iTunes/Finder
backups, accessible on jailbroken devices, and readable by MDM profiles on managed
devices.
The Keychain provides hardware-backed encryption and access control classes:
- .whenUnlocked — only when device is unlocked (most secure)
- .afterFirstUnlock — survives reboot, accessible in background (use for auth tokens
  that background sync tasks need to read)
- .whenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly — most secure, but not backed up
Commonly misplaced in UserDefaults:
- Auth tokens (appAuthToken, api_key, bearer_token)
- Passwords (savedPassword)
- Session cookies
- API secrets
Acceptable in UserDefaults:
- User preferences (theme, sync interval setting)
- Last sync date timestamps
- Non-sensitive counters
- Feature flags
gotchas: Use .afterFirstUnlock (not .whenUnlocked) for tokens that background sync needs — .whenUnlocked blocks background reads after a reboot
Always call SecItemDelete before SecItemAdd (upsert pattern) — SecItemAdd fails with errSecDuplicateItem if the key already exists
Don't forget to handle the migration from UserDefaults to Keychain on first launch after upgrade — read from UserDefaults, write to Keychain, delete from UserDefaults
Passwords should never be stored anywhere after initial login — re-authenticate via token only, never re-send password from storage

entries.title: iOS - Persistent Logging Must Sanitize PII Before Storage or Transmission
entries.summary:
When replacing raw print() calls with a persistent logger that writes to disk or
ships to a backend, always audit for PII in existing log messages first. Common
violations: auth tokens in "Starting sync with token: X", GPS coords in location
logs, health values, device names.
entries.details:
The migration from print() to a persistent logger seems safe because print() already
outputs to the Xcode console. But print() is ephemeral — it disappears when the
process ends. A persistent logger writes to disk (survives kills, accessible in
backups) and potentially ships to a server. That changes the threat model.
Common PII found in print()/log statements in iOS apps:
- Auth tokens: "Bearer eyJ..." in API call logs
- Passwords: logged during auth debugging, never cleaned up
- GPS coordinates: lat/lon in location update logs
- Health values: "Uploaded 95 bpm heart rate" — exact values are health data
- User names: from UIDevice.current.name ("John's iPhone") or profile data
- Email: logged in "Logged in as user@example.com"
Mitigation strategy:
1. Define a log sanitizer that strips/redacts sensitive patterns
2. Categorize logs by sensitivity (category: sync|location|health|api|app)
3. Apply different retention and shipping rules per category:
   - app/sync: can ship to backend freely
   - location: ship coordinates as fuzzy (round to 2 decimal places) or omit
   - health: never ship raw values — ship event type only ("steps sync: N points")
   - api: strip Bearer tokens from URLs and headers before logging
4. Review all existing print() calls before migrating — don't blindly wrap in logger
gotchas: UIDevice.current.name is personal (often "John's iPhone") — use UIDevice.current.model instead for device context in crash reporters
GPS coordinates logged at full precision (6 decimal places) are as sensitive as health data — fuzz or omit in shipped logs
Test the sanitizer against your actual log corpus, not just hypothetical inputs
Log rotation and shipping are separate concerns — you can persist locally without shipping, or ship without full persistence

entries.title: Upgrading gt, bd (beads), and dolt
entries.solution:
# Check current versions
gt version
bd version
dolt version
# Upgrade bd and dolt (Homebrew)
brew upgrade beads dolt
# Upgrade gt (rebuild from source — always gets latest committed code)
cd ~/gt/gastown/mayor/rig
git pull
make install
# This rebuilds, signs, installs to ~/.local/bin/gt, restarts daemon, and syncs plugins.
# Verify
gt version && bd version && dolt version
entries.lesson:
gt is built from source (gastown repo). bd and dolt install via Homebrew.
These should be checked and updated periodically.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Context Sharing
entries.solution:
Use Rally Tavern gossip for ephemeral shared context.
Use knowledge/ for permanent collective intelligence.
Include context field in bounties with relevant intel.
entries.lesson:
When multiple agents work on related tasks, they need shared context.
Without it, agents duplicate work or make conflicting decisions.
